note: min+gz budgets in bytes, enforced by scripts/size-check.mjs (esbuild bundle via the published exports map, minify, gzip -9). The DEFAULT rule is measured + 2%, and a budget derives from the sweep that set it, never from whatever the `baseline` block below it currently reads. Three gated rows depart from the default and say so in their own note: `core-base` uses the base-successor drift rule (measured + 32 B), `core-base-icu` is frozen at 7680 pending the release captain's post-0.5.0 ratchet, and `core-full-composite` is an owner-signed hard ceiling with no automatic margin at all. `baseline` blocks record the last measured numbers behind a budget — they are evidence, not gates. Entries with pending:true are declared slots a later phase graduates; the gate skips them with the notice in `pendingReason` and they gate nothing until the flag is dropped. Informational entries (no gzipBudgetBytes) are measured and printed, never gated. `external` keeps framework peer deps out of a fixture's bundle so the framework fixtures measure the comvi graph only. `sentinelModules` + `expectSentinels` assert module-graph membership from the esbuild metafile (module IDs, never output text); `node scripts/size-check.mjs --modules` prints the full comvi module list behind those fixtures. framework-slim tier-3 A (.omc/handoffs/fs-tier3.md §1) re-baselined EVERY row in one sweep: `useDefineForClassFields: false` removes the __publicField lowering from all 35 I18n class fields, which is -191 B min+gz on each core entry and -174..-200 B on each framework fixture. No fixture's graph changed, so budgets were recomputed from the new measurements under the unchanged convention (`slim` = measured + 32 B drift, every other gated row = measured + 2%, `full` frozen at the USER-signed 8598 — HISTORICAL, superseded by the 8605 ceiling on `core-full-composite` — and `slim-icu` frozen at 7680). framework-slim tier-3 B (.omc/handoffs/fs-tier3.md §2) then re-baselined every row a SECOND time, for the clean-trio capability extraction (C1 devtools discovery -> the new `@comvi/core/devtools` subpath, C5a tag-grammar entities/escape -> the tags extension, C6 nested-catalog flattening -> the loader capability + the pure `flattenCatalog` export). The slim family drops again; the ROOT and root-host fixtures rise 38-65 B because the root entry, batteries-included at the time, composed all three capabilities back in across chunk boundaries — they still measure 114-135 B BELOW the pre-tier-3 anchor, so gate G5 (root-host fixtures must not regress >2%) is satisfied by improvement, not by margin. framework-slim(perf) then restored the root constructor's first-catalog-write fast path (.omc/handoffs/ctor-perf.md): +6..+11 B min+gz on every core-dependent row (slim 4902 -> 4909, full 8385 -> 8397), 0 over budget. Deliberately NOT re-baselined — absorbing a change this small is exactly what the 32 B slim drift margin and the 2% margin on every other row are for, so budgets and their `baseline` anchors keep deriving from the tier-3 B sweep above. single-entry P1 then re-baselined the core family ONCE more, for the convergence itself: `slim*` rows became `core-base*` (the root IS that host now), `full` became `core-full-composite` (the 0.4 semantics recomposed with `.with(...)` in the parity order), `fw-next-root` became `fw-next-composed-factory` (the published root through a non-exported builder), and two informational `/icu`-installer rows were added. One property of this corpus was measured during that landing and is worth knowing before chasing a byte: a row's gzip figure moves by ~1 B per imported content-hashed chunk name when ANY source edit changes those hash characters, while the minified payload does not change. The core build is deterministic (three consecutive builds produce an identical md5), so such a swing is not flakiness and not weight — it is why `core-full-composite` carries a stated 1 B allowance inside its owner-signed ceiling and nothing else does. ONE AUTHORITATIVE RUN: every `baseline` block in the core family and `fw-next-composed-factory` below is the same landed `node scripts/size-check.mjs` run — `core-base` 5016/13494, `core-base-tags` 5977/16106, `core-base-icu` 5890/15794, `core-base-loader` 6545/18207, `core-base-icu-tags` 6805/18409, `core-base-loader-tags` 7382/20494, `core-full-composite` 8604/23957, `fw-next-composed-factory` 10115/28056. Every other figure in these notes is provenance for a budget or a superseded measurement, and is labelled HISTORICAL where it could be read as current.
